Explanation

Your application has hardcoded URLs that might correspond to services that are not accessible on Azure.

Review and ensure that the application is attempting to access URLs that would be available from Azure. You might need to migrate those services to Azure too, this way you will get the benefit of lower latency in the cloud.

If your application needs to depend on services that run on-premises, you can connect your Azure and local networks with ExpressRoute, Hybrid Connections, or VPN solutions.
Local or network IO operations detected
 Potential 3
FilePosition
src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.csLine 57
src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.csLine 57

Explanation

Your application has local or network IO operations.

If you are targeting Managed Instance on Azure App Service, move persistent I/O to storage mounts (Azure Files/UNC). Keep local writes to temp only; connect to external dependencies via private endpoints/VNet to reduce latency.

IO operations outside of the application folder might not be available on Azure App Service. Review and ensure IO APIs are attempting to access paths that will be available when your app is running on App Service sandbox. If you choose the containerized hosting option, your scenario still might be broken or have scalability issues.

Possible solutions:
1. Files that the application needs can be deployed with the application or put in Azure Storage. You can use Azure Storage File Shares as a drop-in replacement for on-premises file share.
2. Other services that the application depends on might need to be migrated to Azure, this way you will get the benefit of lower latency in the cloud.
3. If your application needs to depend on services that run on-premise, you can connect your Azure and local networks with ExpressRoute, Hybrid Connections, or VPN solutions.
Local OS environment access detected
 Potential 1
FilePosition
src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.csLine 56
src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.csLine 56

Explanation

Local OS environment access detected.

If you are targeting Managed Instance on Azure App Service, Read config via App Settings or App Configuration; avoid machine‑specific environment APIs. Persist environment setup via install scripts when needed.

When running in Azure App Service environment, your application can read environment variables that you define in App Service settings. Using environment API other than reading environment variables might indicate that your application depends on some local machine's features and might be broken on App Service sandbox or not scale well. Review your scenarios and either refactor them to be more cloud friendly or choose the option in App Service to host your application in the sandbox for Windows Container Web Apps.

If you choose to use other Azure hosting options such as Azure Container Apps (ACA) or Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), environment APIs might work, however scaling still might be an issue.
SQL database connection detected
 Potential 3
FilePosition
src\eShopWCFService\Web.config

Explanation

SQL database connection detected.

Ensure the database is available/reachable on Azure.

If it is not, there are multiple ways you can move your data to Azure:
1. Migrate to Azure SQL Database.
2. Consider Azure SQL Managed Instance if you need features that are not available in Azure SQL Database and you don’t want to use a VM.
3. Migrate your database servers directly to SQL Server on Azure VMs.

To assess database migration effort, you can use Azure Migrate tool, see the link below.

Explanation

Connection strings without configuration builders detected.

Keeping connection strings directly in the app is not the best practice and might introduce security risks, increased maintenance, scalability challenges or compliance standards (such as PCI DSS, GDPR, etc.).

Instead, it is recommended to use configuration builders to get secrets from secure sources in Azure environment.

Your current approach of serving static content directly might lead to increased costs, performance issues, maintenance challenges (requiring application redeployment for content changes), and security risks.

Consider moving static content to Azure Blob Storage and adding Azure CDN.
Upgrade to newer target framework to get better cloud experience
 Optional 3
FilePosition
src\eShopWCFService\eShopWCFService.csproj

Explanation

Upgrade to newer target framework to get better cloud experience.

If you are targeting Managed Instance on Azure App Service, validate on .NET Framework 4.8 or move to .NET 10. Persist any runtime prerequisites via install scripts; test in staging before production.

While if targeting other Azure compute services:

Application targeting .NET framework lower than 4.7.1 might missing features that would be needed for some cloud scenarios like scaling or getting secrets from secure external sources.

Azure App Service runs apps on .NET Framework 4.8 or .NET Framework 3.5. Apps running on on .NET Framework versions older than .NET Framework 4.8 could have potential compatibility issues. It is recommended to test your application running on .NET Framework 4.8. Note that it is not necessary to re-target to .NET Framework 4.8, only to validate that the app correctly runs on that version of .NET Framework.

In the long term it is also recommended to upgrade your application to latest supported .NET 8+ which would significantly increase performance of your application. Use tools like .NET Upgrade Assistant to help with upgrading your application to newer .NET.
System.Data.SqlClient dependency detected
 Optional 3
FilePosition
src\eShopWCFService\Web.config

Explanation

System.Data.SqlClient dependency is detected.

While System.Data.SqlClient will work in Azure, the newer Microsoft.Data.SqlClient package is the primary .NET SQL client moving forward and receiving the latest features. For example, Microsoft.Data.SqlClient easily allows use of Azure Managed Identity from a connection string.

Explanation

API is binary incompatible for selected .NET version: affects existing binaries, often requiring recompilation, because the API has changed in a way that prevents older binaries from loading or executing.
Project's target framework(s) needs to be changed
 Mandatory 1
FilePosition
src\eShopWCFService\eShopWCFService.csproj
src\eShopWinForms\eShopWinForms.csproj

Explanation

Project's target framework(s) needs to be changed to the new target framework that you selected for this upgrade.

During upgrade target framework will be adjusted to corresponding platform when applicable. In some cases project would result in multiple target frameworks after the upgrade if it was using features that now have their own platforms in modern .NET frameworks (windows, iOS, Android etc).
Project file needs to be converted to SDK-style
 Mandatory 1
FilePosition
src\eShopWCFService\eShopWCFService.csproj

Explanation

Project file needs to be converted to SDK-style. Modern .NET framework projects require a change in the project file format and use SDK corresponding to project flavor and functionality.
WCF Client APIs
 Mandatory 1
FilePosition

Explanation

WCF client-side APIs for building service clients that communicate with WCF services. These APIs are available as exact equivalents via NuGet packages - add System.ServiceModel.* NuGet packages (System.ServiceModel.Http, System.ServiceModel.Primitives, System.ServiceModel.NetTcp, etc.)
Legacy Configuration System
 Mandatory 2
FilePosition

Explanation

Legacy XML-based configuration system (app.config/web.config) that has been replaced by a more flexible configuration model in .NET Core. The old system was rigid and XML-based. Migrate to Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration with JSON/environment variables; use System.Configuration.ConfigurationManager NuGet package as interim bridge if needed.
GDI+ / System.Drawing
 Mandatory 1
FilePosition

Explanation

System.Drawing APIs for 2D graphics, imaging, and printing that are available via NuGet package System.Drawing.Common. Note: Not recommended for server scenarios due to Windows dependencies; consider cross-platform alternatives like SkiaSharp or ImageSharp for new code.
Windows Forms Legacy Controls
 Mandatory 3
FilePosition

Explanation

Legacy Windows Forms controls that have been removed from .NET Core/5+ including StatusBar, DataGrid, ContextMenu, MainMenu, MenuItem, and ToolBar. These controls were replaced by more modern alternatives. Use ToolStrip, MenuStrip, ContextMenuStrip, and DataGridView instead.
Windows Forms
 Mandatory 1
FilePosition

Explanation

Architecture Diagram

Static assessment scoped exclusively to eShopModernizedNTier; all evidence paths are relative to that workspace. The solution contains a Windows desktop client and an IIS-hosted catalog service, with SQL Server as the persistent store (eShopModernizedNTier.sln:6-11).

Data Storage & External Services

The service owns one SQL Server database; its environment-provided connection overrides a named LocalDB fallback (src\eShopWCFService\Models\Infrastructure\CatalogConfiguration.cs:10-17). Compose declares the service and SQL Server, but no cache, broker, identity provider, or external business API (docker-compose.yml:3-13). Images are desktop-local files, not a remote image service (src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.cs:55-61). This is source/configuration evidence, not proof of a running deployment.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • Manual composition connects a generated proxy, controller, and view; constructor injection is used without an active DI container (src\eShopWinForms\Program.cs:22-27; src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:14-20). The apparent registration module is commented out, not an active mock switch (src\eShopWinForms\Modules\ApplicationModule.cs:12-34).
  • Business operations access DbContext directly, with no separate repository layer. Missing-database creation and programmatic seeding replace a migration pipeline (src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:16-25; src\eShopWCFService\Models\Infrastructure\CatalogDBInitializer.cs:11-20).
  • The deployed contract is SOAP, not REST; the default desktop proxy hardcodes an HTTP loopback destination (src\eShopWCFService\Web.config:37-40; src\eShopWinForms\Connected Services\eShopServiceReference\Reference.cs:591-609). Remote deployment requires explicit endpoint configuration changes.

Entity fields and mapping are in data-architecture.md. No OpenAPI, protobuf, or GraphQL schema was found in the scoped file inventory.

Communication Patterns

  • Synchronous: UI events call the controller, then the generated proxy, then SOAP service operations. The controller uses synchronous methods even though generated Async variants exist (src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:35-54,75-84; generated proxy Reference.cs:501-508).
  • Composition: The desktop separately fetches catalog items and today's discount, then combines them for display. It is not gateway aggregation and involves only one business service (src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:75-84).
  • Resilience: No application retry, circuit breaker, bulkhead, fallback, or explicit timeout value is configured in the inspected controller/proxy binding. Platform timeout defaults are not restated as source configuration. Failure interrupts the caller; mock data is not an automatic fallback (src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:35-84; generated proxy Reference.cs:591-600; src\eShopWinForms\Modules\ApplicationModule.cs:12-34).
  • Discovery: No registry/load balancer; the default generated client uses a hardcoded loopback URL. Constructor overloads allow alternate addresses, but Program selects the default constructor (src\eShopWinForms\Program.cs:23; generated proxy Reference.cs:448-477,605-609).
  • Startup: SQL must be usable before service database access; desktop initialization requires service availability. Compose ordering does not guarantee readiness. See configuration-inventory.md.
  • Security posture: No application authentication or authorization checks are present in the service contract/implementation. The active endpoint and default client use plain HTTP basicHttpBinding without an explicit security mode; HTTPS protocol mapping and metadata flags do not prove enforced TLS on the deployed endpoint (src\eShopWCFService\Web.config:27-40; generated proxy Reference.cs:595-609). External IIS policy is not established by this assessment. Exception details in SOAP faults are disabled (Web.config:29).
  • Other protocols: No broker/events are used by the inspected paths. NetTcp and Duplex package references alone do not prove those protocols are active.

Startup Dependency Chain

  1. External Windows network nat must already exist for the root override (docker-compose.override.yml:22-25).
  2. eshopwcfservice → depends on → sql.data, using simple Compose depends_on, not a service_healthy condition (docker-compose.yml:9-10).
  3. SQL healthcheck runs sqlcmd with masked credential arguments and select 1; root interval is 1 second with 20 retries. Temp CI also specifies 20 retries; temp override specifies interval only. No explicit healthcheck timeout/start period is supplied (docker-compose.override.yml:17-20; temp\docker-compose.ci.build.yml:15-18; temp\docker-compose.override.yml:15-17). These settings do not create a service-readiness gate for the simple depends_on.
  4. First server data access can create/seed a missing database; no custom connection retry/wait loop was found (src\eShopWCFService\EntityModel.cs:12-15; src\eShopWCFService\Models\Infrastructure\CatalogDBInitializer.cs:11-20).
  5. Desktop LoadView calls the service before showing its modal UI; no readiness retry/fallback wraps this initialization (src\eShopWinForms\Program.cs:26-27; src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:150-157).

Core Business Workflows

The application lets operators browse merchandise with date-based promotional pricing, inspect daily stock, and record product availability for an arrival date. These workflows are traced only within eShopModernizedNTier; evidence paths below are relative to that workspace.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
CatalogItemCatalogService / CatalogMerchandise displayed to the operatorCategorized by brand and product type; referenced by stock records
CatalogBrandCatalogService / CatalogBrand lookup used for filteringClassifies merchandise
CatalogTypeCatalogService / CatalogProduct-category lookup used for filteringClassifies merchandise
CatalogItemsStockCatalogService / AvailabilityAvailability recorded for an item on a calendar dayLogical reference to merchandise
DiscountItemCatalogService / PromotionsA time-bounded catalog-wide discount fractionApplied to displayed merchandise, not linked to individual products

Evidence: src\eShopWCFService\Models\CatalogItem.cs:11-35; Models\CatalogBrand.cs:11-19, Models\CatalogType.cs:11-19, Models\CatalogItemsStock.cs:12-25, Models\DiscountItem.cs:12-31, all under src\eShopWCFService; application use at src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:35-84. These are functional groupings within one service, not independently deployed bounded-context services.

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
CatalogServiceCatalog, availability, promotionsAll five domain entitiesService-owned persistence (src\eShopWCFService\EntityModel.cs:18-22)
Desktop CatalogController / CatalogViewOperator interaction and display compositionNo authoritative persistent entities; contract copies onlyCatalogService and local product images (src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:35-84; src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.cs:55-61)

The service is the source of truth for stock and catalog data. The desktop computes displayed discounts but does not persist discounted prices. No cross-service domain-event ownership or shared aggregate transaction is implemented in the traced code.

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Browse catalog with active promotional pricing

  1. Startup constructs the view and service client, connects the controller, and loads initial data before displaying the window (src\eShopWinForms\Program.cs:22-27).
  2. LoadView initializes the discount banner, catalog, brand/type filters, and shipment product selectors (src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:150-157).
  3. Changing either filter raises an event; the controller reloads the catalog using the All-filter rule (src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.cs:106-135; src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:27-29,75-78).
  4. The service selects matching products. The desktop requests today's discount separately and applies the Promotional-date rule and Display-price rule (src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:28-30,56-62; src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:79-84).
  5. The view renders each price and local thumbnail. With no active promotion, original prices are shown; local image-file or service errors have no implemented fallback in this path (src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.cs:48-61).

Workflow 2: Record availability and inspect daily stock

  1. Operator selects a product, quantity, and arrival date. The Shipment-input rule gates submission (src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.cs:157-167).
  2. Controller constructs a stock request and sends it to the service (src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:35-42).
  3. Service finds any stock record for the product/calendar day. Under the Daily-stock replacement rule, it replaces an existing quantity or inserts a new record, then persists it (src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:99-117).
  4. Only after the call returns does the controller notify success; the view displays a message and clears shipment inputs (src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:42-43; src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.cs:189-195).
  5. For a stock inquiry, the selected product and calendar date are sent to the service. The Missing-stock rule determines the result, which is appended to the stock results list (src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.cs:142-151,173-178; src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:50-54; src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:90-96).

Although the UI calls this a shipment, it records a daily availability total, not an additive shipment ledger. There is no order placement, reservation, payment, or fulfillment workflow in these sources.

Workflow 3: Initialize demonstration business data

On first data use, a missing database is created and seeded with product classifications, merchandise, availability, and promotions (src\eShopWCFService\EntityModel.cs:12-15; src\eShopWCFService\Models\Infrastructure\CatalogDBInitializer.cs:11-20). Seed stock/promotion dates are in 2017, so the seed promotions do not cover the assessment date; existing databases are not automatically refreshed (src\eShopWCFService\Models\Infrastructure\PreconfiguredData.cs:41-50,65-74). No scheduler or background job advances promotional periods.

Cross-Service Data Flows

There is one business service and one desktop consumer, not a gateway with multiple downstream services. The controller joins catalog and promotion responses in memory for display; each product's base price is combined with a single selected global discount fraction (src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:75-84). Stock requests correlate to products by identifier, and thumbnails correlate to a local filename (src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:37-42; src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.cs:55-61).

No circuit breaker, automatic mock substitution, compensating workflow, or partial-response recovery is implemented. A missing promotion is a normal business branch, not an outage fallback; a service failure propagates from the synchronous calls (src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:35-84). The mock's discount operation itself throws and is not selected by Program (src\eShopWCFService\CatalogServiceMock.cs:118-120; src\eShopWinForms\Program.cs:23).

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant Operator as "Catalog operator" participant View as "Availability form" participant Controller as "Desktop coordinator" participant Service as "Catalog service" participant Stock as "Daily stock records" Operator->>View: Select merchandise and enter arrival quantity and date alt Required shipment inputs present View->>View: Parse shipment input View->>Controller: Submit daily availability Controller->>Service: Record availability for product and day Service->>Stock: Find matching daily stock Stock-->>Service: Existing record or none alt Existing daily record Service->>Stock: Replace quantity and save else New product day Service->>Stock: Assign new record identity and save end Stock-->>Service: Save completed Service-->>Controller: Completion Controller->>View: Confirm availability recorded View-->>Operator: Success message and cleared inputs else Required shipment inputs absent Note over View: Return without sending a request end Note over Controller,Stock: Parse or service failure has no implemented retry or fallback Operator->>View: Inspect product stock on selected day View->>Controller: Request daily stock Controller->>Service: Look up daily availability Service->>Stock: Find matching daily stock Stock-->>Service: Existing quantity or none alt Daily record exists Service-->>Controller: Recorded quantity else No daily record Service-->>Controller: Zero end Controller->>View: Append availability result View-->>Operator: Daily stock result

The sequence follows Workflow 2's cited implementation. Decision blocks show actual input/record branches, not an invented circuit breaker.

Business Rules & Decision Logic

RuleImplemented decision / constraintEvidence
All-filter ruleFilter ID zero means all brands/types; nonzero filters are combined with AND. The desktop inserts an All option with ID zero.src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:56-62; src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:103-115,129-141
Promotional-date ruleMatch calendar dates inclusively from start through end; take first matching promotion. No priority/overlap arbitration is specified.src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:28-30
Display-price ruleDisplay base price multiplied by one minus discount fraction, using double conversion and fixed-point formatting; banner percentage rounds fraction times 100. No persisted price change occurs.src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.cs:48-61; src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:60-68
Shipment-input ruleReturn if no selected product, empty quantity, or empty date; otherwise use int.Parse and Convert.ToDateTime. No TryParse/culture override or positivity/date-range validation is implemented.src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.cs:157-167
Daily-stock replacement ruleMatch product and calendar day; replace quantity, never add to it. Otherwise insert using largest stock key plus one. No uniqueness check beyond first-match application logic.src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:99-117
Missing-stock ruleMissing daily record returns zero, indistinguishable from an explicitly recorded zero.src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:90-96
Stock-inquiry selectionAssumes a product is selected and its label can be parsed; no null guard is present.src\eShopWinForms\Views\CatalogView.cs:142-150
Entity-level constraintsBrand/type text annotations set maximum length 50; no explicit required/range constraints for price, discount fraction, or stock are declared in the inspected models.src\eShopWCFService\Models\CatalogBrand.cs:17; src\eShopWCFService\Models\CatalogType.cs:17; Models\CatalogItem.cs:13-35, Models\CatalogItemsStock.cs:14-25, Models\DiscountItem.cs:18-31 under src\eShopWCFService
Product identity allocationCreation uses maximum current ID plus one, without an empty-table or concurrent-create branch.src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:65-70
  • Transactions and consistency: Each mutation saves locally; there is no explicit transaction spanning lookup plus Max allocation or multiple service calls. Concurrent requests can race on stock upsert or manually allocated identities (src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:65-82,99-117).
  • Lifecycle: Stock is created or overwritten; no shipment state machine, reservation lifecycle, approval state, or historical adjustment audit is modeled in the five entity declarations.
  • Errors and compensation: No business-specific exception contract, controller recovery, compensation, or dead-letter mechanism appears in these paths. Fault exception-detail output is disabled (src\eShopWCFService\Web.config:29).
  • Authorization and audit: No role, resource-owner, or business authorization checks or business audit logging appear in the traced service methods (src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:28-117). External host policies and database auditing are not established.

These are source-traced behaviors and limitations, not results from an execution test.

Version & Compatibility Risks

The mixed .NET 6 desktop / .NET Framework 4.6.1 server targets and alternate 4.7.1 client require different build/runtime tooling. .NET 6 and .NET Framework 4.6.1 are out of support as of this assessment; package patch levels are old, but no vulnerability lookup or compatibility build was performed. EF6-to-EF Core and WCF-server-to-modern-.NET changes are not simple target-framework substitutions. Evidence: target declarations above; server imports classic web application targets (src\eShopWCFService\eShopWCFService.csproj:115-117).

Notable Observations

  • The solution selects eShopWinForms.csproj, not eShopWinForms.fx.csproj; alternate-project dependencies are explicitly included here to avoid hiding legacy declarations (eShopModernizedNTier.sln:8-10).
  • EF package versions differ between server and active desktop; WebApi.Client versions differ between the two desktop project files. Counts deduplicate package IDs, not declarations.
  • No central package management, dependency lockfile, or test package declaration was found among the scoped build files. Full transitive versions cannot be recovered from direct declarations alone.
  • Docker tooling uses Microsoft.Docker.Sdk without a pinned SDK version; it is build infrastructure, not an additional application NuGet dependency (docker-compose.dcproj:2).

Data Architecture & Persistence Layer

Five EF6 entity sets represent catalog products, brands, types, daily stock, and discount periods in SQL Server. This source-based assessment is scoped to eShopModernizedNTier; paths are workspace-relative (src\eShopWCFService\EntityModel.cs:10-22).

Each SaveChanges has EF's ordinary local transaction semantics; no explicit encompassing transaction or cross-call transaction is defined. Max-plus-one allocation is not concurrency-safe and Max on an empty set is not handled. No bulk cross-service query or stored procedure was found.

Caching Strategy

No Redis, MemoryCache, distributed cache, result-cache TTL, or second-level cache is declared in the scoped dependencies/configuration. EF change tracking is context-local identity tracking, not a shared query cache; repeated calls materialize lists anew (src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:28-30,46-62). CatalogServiceMock holds seed lists but is not a production cache or automatic fallback (src\eShopWCFService\CatalogServiceMock.cs:18-23; src\eShopWinForms\Program.cs:23).

Data Ownership Boundaries

One business service owns one catalog store; this is not database-per-microservice or a multi-service shared-database design. The desktop accesses data through the generated SOAP contract and composes item/discount results locally (src\eShopWinForms\Controllers\CatalogController.cs:75-84). Reads and writes share the same DbContext/entity model; no CQRS, outbox, broker replication, or cross-service database joins were found (src\eShopWCFService\EntityModel.cs:18-22; src\eShopWCFService\CatalogService.svc.cs:28-117).
